title: Can LLMs Maintain Fundamental Abilities under KV Cache Compression?
one_line_claim: KV-cache compression causes task-dependent performance degradation across fundamental LLM abilities (arithmetic reasoning, long-context generation most vulnerable), with chunk-level methods and shot-level semantic preservation offering mitigation.
method_summary: KVFundaBench systematically evaluates KV-cache compression across five fundamental capability categories (world knowledge, commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, code generation, safety) and long-context understanding, using metrics like relative performance change across compression methods (StreamingLLM, H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, ChunkKV). Attention pattern analysis reveals task-specific vulnerabilities, with arithmetic and generation tasks showing more diffuse attention requiring broader context preservation. ShotKV proposes separate prefill and decoding compression strategies that preserve shot-level semantic coherence, achieving superior performance on long-context reasoning.

key_findings.quote: Arithmetic reasoning, code generation, and safety tasks demonstrate the highest compression sensitivity, characterized by precipitous performance declines. Figure 5 illustrates the detailed performance impact of various KV cache compression methods across different tasks. This degradation is most pronounced in arithmetic reasoning (c), where performance deteriorates significantly below the compression ratio of 20%, with precision dropping from approximately 0.75 to below 0.5.
key_findings.finding: Arithmetic reasoning tasks demonstrate the highest compression sensitivity, with performance declining significantly below 30% compression ratio, while world knowledge and commonsense reasoning maintain stability above 40% compression ratios.

key_findings.quote: Long-Context Generation Sensitivity: KV cache compression exhibits significant performance degradation in long-context generation tasks. As demonstrated in Table 3, the evaluation of three unified compression methods, StreamingLLM, H2O, and PyramidInferer on LG-GSM8K reveals substantial performance limitations. In this arithmetic reasoning task with approximately 4k token generation duration, compression methods show notable deterioration, with performance declining by more than 20% at compression ratios below 30%.
key_findings.finding: Long-context generation tasks are particularly affected by KV-cache compression, with substantial performance deterioration at compression ratios below 30%, revealing that generation capabilities degrade more than 20% at ratios below 30%.

key_findings.quote: Chunk-Level Superiority: Chunk-level compression is more effective for long-context structured reasoning tasks. Inspired by Agarwal et al. [44], we consider many-shot in-context learning as a long-context reasoning task, which is more complex than existing long-context benchmarks, such as LongBench and NIAH. Figure 6 shows the performance of KV cache compression methods on a 50-shot GSM8K task, where the prompt length exceeds 4K tokens. From the figure, we observe that ChunkKV [42] demonstrates the most stability when the compression ratio is below 10% on both LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, indicating that in more complex long-context arithmetic reasoning tasks, chunk-level retention is more effective at preserving semantic information.
key_findings.finding: Chunk-level compression is more effective than token-level approaches for preserving long-context structured reasoning, with ChunkKV demonstrating superior stability on long-context arithmetic tasks compared to token-level methods.

key_findings.quote: ShotKV achieves the best performance on many-shot Arithmetic Reasoning on LG-GSM8K, maintaining high performance at low compression ratios. Even in aggressive compression settings (25%-30%), ShotKV maintains relatively stable performance (26.83%-38.33%), while other methods experience more severe degradation (6.33%-16.67%). And Table 3 shows that ShotKV achieves 9%-18% performance improvements on long-context generation tasks under aggressive compression ratios.
key_findings.finding: ShotKV achieves 9%-18% performance improvements on long-context generation tasks under aggressive compression ratios by preserving complete shot examples during prefill and applying dynamic compression during decoding.

key_findings.quote: Prompt Length Vulnerability: Shorter prompts are more vulnerable to KV cache compression. As illustrated in Figure 8, the effect of KV cache compression is markedly different with varying prompt lengths (shot numbers). Scenarios with fewer shots (for example, one-shot and two-shot) demonstrate heightened sensitivity to compression; their performance degrades more precipitously below a compression ratio of 30%. For example, in 1-shot settings, performance decreases from 0.5 to 0.05 as the compression ratio decreases from 30% to 10%. In contrast, 8-shot settings experience a less severe reduction, from 0.75 to 0.5 under the same compression conditions.
key_findings.finding: Shorter prompts (1-2 shot) demonstrate heightened sensitivity to compression, with performance degradation accelerating below 30% compression ratio, while 8-shot scenarios show more resilience with less severe reduction.

relation_to_herald.shared: Both papers investigate failure modes induced by KV-cache compression during LLM generation Both recognize that compression is a critical system bottleneck requiring intervention Both propose methods to predict or detect performance degradation from runtime signals rather than offline metrics
differs_on: This paper evaluates fundamental capability degradation (world knowledge, reasoning, code generation, safety) across diverse compression methods at scale; HERALD targets catastrophic structural failures (looping, non-termination, instruction amnesia) in specific compression scenarios

This paper uses task-level performance metrics (accuracy, pass rate) to characterize compression sensitivity; HERALD uses per-token logit features and XGBoost to forecast hazards at prediction horizon H tokens ahead
This paper proposes ShotKV as a compression method improvement; HERALD proposes a runtime predictor for downstream systems to intervene, treating compression as a black box
